title: customer-integration-stitch-notes-2026-12-22
content:
Attendees: Aisha (SE lead), Marco (Field Eng), Dana (ProServices PM), Priya (SRE), Ethan (Solutions Eng), + 2 customer TPMs dialed in for Veridian and Tidewater

Agenda:
- Quick status + bright spots
- Deep dive on Veridian inference slowdown
- Tidewater VPC peering checklist & remaining items
- Rollout cadence for Lighthouse canary (small traffic test)
- Action items and owners

High-level summary:
This meeting focused on stitching together remaining integration pieces for Veridian and Tidewater and aligning timelines for Lighthouse canary. Progress is steady but two technical blockers (KV cache warm-up behavior and a quantization mismatch in the customer's self-hosted model variant) are creating risk for Veridian's scheduled go-live. Tidewater is mostly on track pending final network validation and policy docs. We agreed on a tighter escalation window for any new perf regression: 24 hours ETA on mitigation plan.

Customer updates (detailed)
1) Veridian (primary):
- Status: delayed (target go-live 2027-01-14 now at risk)
- What went well: initial model onboarding succeeded, canary harness produced stable outputs for short sequences, telemetry hooked into Console dashboards.
- Blocker: KV cache warm-up causes 3x token latency on first 30s of sustained traffic in Dedicated pool. Observed pattern: cold VM + model variant q4 -> first requests fall back to CPU path intermittently.
- Investigation notes (Priya + Ethan): kernel selection logs show fallback to aten kernels on a small subset of tokens; memory pressure spike correlates with other tenant burst (see JIRA-4892). Hypothesis: autoscaler adds node and migrates workload causing transient reinitialization of KV caches.
- Immediate mitigation tried: pinned a small warm-up job (5 concurrent requests of 256 tokens) prior to traffic cutover; reduced tail latency but not eliminated. Marco to run extended warm-up script nightly until we land config fix.
- Next steps: Engineering to add a KV-cache-preserve flag in deploy agent (rw-deploy PR referenced). ETA for PR review: 2026-12-27 (PR 311). If merged, we target a staged roll 2026-12-29.
- Customer comms: Dana to send an updated go/no-go note by 2026-12-24 clarifying rollback plan and contingency (use hosted fallback model).

2) Tidewater (mid-market):
- Status: green but manual checks remain
- Network: VPC peering established; BGP routes validated. One intermittent packet loss during peak seen on 12/20; root cause appears to be incorrect MTU on an on-prem firewall.
- Security/compliance: customer requested audit export for last 90 days; solution: enable S3 export -> Dana to own and deliver by 2026-12-23.
- Ops note: provisioning script for dedicated pool needs one additional IAM role for their infra team. Created JIRA-5021; expected completion 2026-12-23.
- Next steps: small dry-run with 10% traffic on 2026-12-28; Marco to coordinate with customer TPM.

3) Lighthouse (large enterprise pilot):
- Status: planning canary, internal approvals obtained
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% over 72 hours with automatic rollback triggers on >3% increase in latency or any quality regression per eval set.
- Action: solutions eng to define eval prompt set (Priya assigned, due 2026-12-26).

4) Meridian (early integration):
- Status: exploratory; spike completed for embedding pipeline. Potential ask for hosted embeddings SLA. Follow-up: team to propose SLO in next week's sync.

Cross-cutting technical notes:
- Quantization mismatch: Customer Veridian self-hosted model uses a non-standard INT4 packing that our runtime currently interprets as INT8, causing inference errors at long sequence lengths. This was surfaced by their QA tests and intermittently reproduces in our staging. Proposed fix: add a model-inspection step during onboarding to verify quantization metadata and fallback to a verified variant with conversion. Priya/Ethan to prototype conversion script (P0) with ETA 2026-12-30.
- Autoscaler behavior: observed node churn during sustained traffic can disrupt cache locality. Engineering to add a drain/warmup hook to autoscaler so newly created nodes run warm-up jobs before receiving production traffic. Design doc: link (internal) shared in chat.
- Telemetry: we want token-level breakdown in Console for dedicated customers — open product ask for 1Q roadmap. Dana to escalate with product-hosted-api.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Veridian go-live slips beyond business window -> Mitigation: offer hosted-backed SLA for first 2 weeks post-launch; finance approval needed for credit.
- Risk: SRE capacity over holidays (end of year) -> Mitigation: schedule on-call overlap and nominate backup responders (Priya to publish on-call rota by 2026-12-23).

Action items (owner -> due):
- Marco: run extended KV warm-up nightly for Veridian + share results in /#veridian-infra (due: ongoing, first batch 2026-12-23)
- Ethan: prototype kv-cache-preserve flag and push PR + test harness (due: 2026-12-27)
- Priya: prototype quantization-detect-and-convert script; share rough plan in sync (due: 2026-12-30)
- Dana: updated customer comms for Veridian go/no-go; S3 audit export for Tidewater (due: 2026-12-24 and 2026-12-23 respectively)
- Aisha: coordinate finance ask for hosted fallback credit (due: 2026-12-24)
- Marco & Dana: run Tidewater 10% dry-run (due: 2026-12-28)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding a small "pre-warm" autopolicy in Dedicated console for customers coming off cold starts (toggle in UI). Could be product feature for 1Q.
- Look into better model metadata validation at onboarding to prevent INT4/INT8 mismatch surprises. Add to onboarding checklist.
- Revisit holiday escalation policy — explicit backup names, not rotations only.

Open questions for next week:
- Is finance comfortable with offering hosted credit as contingency for Veridian? (Aisha owns)
- Should we fast-track model metadata inspection into onboarding or gate it as a best-effort? Tradeoff with onboarding speed.
- Can Field Eng provide an automated MTU/frag test for on-prem firewalls to catch Tidewater-like issues earlier?

Next sync: 2026-12-29 11:00 PT (short stand)

Appendix (quick refs):
- JIRA-4892: Veridian perf regressions and KV-cache observations
- JIRA-5021: Tidewater IAM provisioning task
- rw-deploy PR #311 (kv-cache-preserve prototype)

End of notes.
